Stated Claim / Post Context:
AI was set up to fail LGBTQIA+ people. Here's how it's already harming us

There is growing evidence of the dangers the technology poses to both democracy and LGBTQIA+ rights

Actual Article Body:
“Artificial Intelligence is going to change our world, that’s inevitable. But in what way it changes our world is still up to us.” I wrote this, about the impact of AI on the queer community, five years ago. This was a time when – if you can believe it – the notion that AI would dominate our world was still novel.

The concerns and experts’ predictions about AI that I laid out in the distant past of 2021 are already having direct impacts on our lives.

One leader in the field who I spoke to all those years ago was anthropologist, media scholar, and 2020 MacArthur Fellow Mary L. Grey, who told me she believed AI would "always fail" the LGBTQIA+ community. Five years later, she tells QueerAF she stands by her words “even more strongly.”

Most AI tools we talk about today, at least in the context of concern or risk, are probabilistic tools, including those we've been investigating: Gemini, ChatGPT and Claude. These tools don't seek 'the right information' and give it to you. They serve it to you based on an estimated probability that it's right, based on previous examples and patterns.

We are a community where we are all significantly different, and have shifting approaches to language, expression and our identities. In an AI machine, this nuance gets lost in what trans researcher Chloe Turner calls "the neutral middle", where answers are accurate in a narrow sense but distorted by the sources they use.

In the trillion-dollar business of AI, the market priority is to serve what as many people as possible want to hear. Marginalised people, by our nature, do not have the numbers to be a priority, and we do not represent the needs of most users.

"AI learns from what shows up most often. So, people and experiences that are less common in the data are easier to miss," Grey says. "This isn’t just a technical bias problem. It’s about who gets to define the categories, goals, and acceptable mistakes when representing our communities. That is the underlying threat to LGBTQIA+ existences – it excludes our diversity, by design."

The major environmental, economic, and community harms of data centres, the misinformation and hallucinations, and the plagiarism and content theft that AI models require all make up the backdrop to this technology – whatever benefits its proponents say it will also have. And without guardrails, it is also a growing danger to both democracy and LGBTQIA+ rights.
